items.title: La coalizione che ha fatto saltare l’accordo alla COP31
items.summary: L'Unione Europea si è unita ai paesi più vulnerabili al cambiamento climatico per evitare un accordo invece di accettarne uno pessimo
items.content:
Per l’opposizione dei paesi produttori di petrolio, il testo oggetto delle trattative non includeva un riferimento all’impegno ad abbandonare i combustibili fossili. Poi però la coalizione ha deciso che un mancato accordo era comunque meglio di un accordo che tornasse indietro rispetto a impegni già presi in passato. Dal punto di vista della diplomazia climatica è stato un fallimento, ma un fallimento di cui dovranno tenere conto le presidenze delle prossime COP, se vorranno impedire che le loro conferenze si concludano senza accordi politici.

La coalizione di 91 paesi, e in particolare quelli dell’Unione Europea, si è presa la responsabilità di far saltare il banco. Non era scontato, visto che l’ultima menzione del petrolio in un testo finale risale alla COP del 2023 a Dubai, in una formulazione molto cauta che invitava i paesi a contribuire alla transizione energetica dai combustibili fossili, senza prevedere obblighi.

Invece di citare i combustibili fossili, il testo proposto dai due paesi che guidavano la conferenza, la Turchia e l’Australia, incoraggiava lo sviluppo delle tecnologie di cattura e stoccaggio dell’anidride carbonica, uno dei principali gas serra, che molti paesi produttori di petrolio e gas promuovono per poter continuare a usare i combustibili fossili. Il riferimento alla transizione era scomparso dal testo giovedì 19 novembre, e il giorno successivo i rappresentanti e i ministri di 23 governi, tra cui quelli di molti paesi europei (l’Italia non c’era) e di altri come Tuvalu, Guatemala e Indonesia, avevano organizzato una conferenza stampa per chiedere che fosse reintegrato nella decisione finale.

Durante la COP31, quegli stessi paesi si erano scontrati duramente su altre questioni, soprattutto su chi dovesse pagare, e quanto, per aiutare i paesi più poveri ad affrontare le conseguenze del riscaldamento globale. Ma si sono ricompattati anche perché sono emerse accuse e sospetti sulla gestione dei negoziati.

Secondo una ricostruzione di Reuters , infatti, alcuni rappresentanti hanno faticato a ottenere incontri con le presidenze turca e australiana, mentre altri paesi hanno avuto accesso frequente ai loro uffici. Tra questi c’era l’Arabia Saudita, che nella seconda settimana era rimasta ferma sull’opposizione al riferimento ai combustibili fossili nell’accordo finale.

Così sabato sera, mentre i funzionari sauditi (e anche quelli cinesi e russi) avevano continuato a incontrare le presidenze, la Germania aveva cominciato a convocare i piccoli stati insulari e i membri della High Ambition Coalition, la Coalizione della Grande Ambizione, che si era formata nel 2015 su impulso dell’allora ministro degli Esteri delle Isole Marshall. La coalizione voleva superare la divisione tra paesi ricchi e paesi in via di sviluppo, formulando delle richieste che potessero mettere tutti d’accordo. Anche grazie a questa strategia era stato raggiunto l’Accordo di Parigi, il trattato internazionale adottato nel 2015 che ha l’obiettivo di mantenere l’aumento della temperatura media globale al di sotto dei 2 °C rispetto a prima dell’industrializzazione.

Dai colloqui organizzati dalla Germania sabato è uscita una lettera sostenuta da 130 paesi, che affermava un principio: qualsiasi accordo finale avrebbe dovuto nominare esplicitamente la transizione dai combustibili fossili.

Palau, un piccolo stato insulare del Pacifico, aveva per esempio sostenuto l’approvazione del testo perché nonostante tutti i suoi difetti conteneva progressi sull’elettrificazione, riconosceva gli effetti del cambiamento climatico sugli oceani, sulle comunità costiere e sulla biodiversità e fissava l’obiettivo di triplicare i finanziamenti per l’adattamento climatico.

Quella dei 91 paesi della coalizione è una posizione comune, che però deriva da bisogni e interessi molto diversi. I più numerosi erano i 44 paesi meno sviluppati, alcuni tra i paesi più poveri al mondo, che chiedevano soprattutto più finanziamenti. C’erano poi i sette paesi dell’AILAC, l’Associazione indipendente dell’America Latina e dei Caraibi, che sono economie in via di sviluppo come Cile, Colombia e Panama: pur rivendicando maggiori finanziamenti, sostengono obiettivi ambiziosi sulla riduzione delle emissioni.

Altri paesi che si sono uniti alla coalizione sono quelli del Gruppo per l’integrità ambientale, al quale aderiscono tra gli altri Svizzera, Messico e Corea del Sud, i cui governi non si riconoscono pienamente nei grandi blocchi tradizionali delle COP. Ma i gruppi più visibili della coalizione sono stati due: quello dei paesi insulari, preoccupati di come poter continuare ad abitare il proprio territorio, e il blocco dei paesi europei, i 27 dell’Unione più Regno Unito e Norvegia, che insistevano soprattutto sull’evitare un passo indietro.

Anche se il Patto di Antalya non è stato approvato, alla COP31 sono comunque state approvate delle decisioni, come quella sul Global Goal on Adaptation, l’obiettivo con cui si cerca di misurare e rafforzare la capacità dei paesi di proteggersi dagli effetti del riscaldamento globale, e una sul programma di lavoro per la finanza climatica.

items.title: Come non detto: Jensen Huang torna alla guida di Nvidia undici giorni dopo le dimissioni
items.summary: Il consiglio di amministrazione lo ha reintegrato all'unanimità dopo aver sentito il governo americano. Prosegue però l'indagine interna sul presunto tentativo di spionaggio cinese ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Jensen Huang è di nuovo presidente e amministratore delegato di Nvidia , oltre che membro del consiglio di amministrazione. Il board ha votato all'unanimità per il reintegro dopo una serie di incontri con Huang, al termine dei quali si è detto convinto della sua franchezza e della sua capacità di guidare la società. Il consiglio ha affermato inoltre di aver ricevuto indicazioni da alti livelli del governo degli Stati Uniti, e sulla base di queste ha ritetenuto che il ritorno di Huang non comporti rischi per la sicurezza nazionale.

Huang si era dimesso il 12 novembre. L'8 novembre il board aveva aperto un'indagine indipendente dopo che il New York Times aveva rivelato la sua relazione con Alice Huang, ex dirigente di Megaspeed. Secondo l'intelligence americana, la donna (che non ha alcuna parentela con Jensen Huang) avrebbe raccolto informazioni per Pechino. Accuse respinte dalla Cina.

L'11 novembre lo stesso quotidiano aveva riferito di una seconda relazione, con una dipendente che riportava direttamente a lui. Martedì scorso, durante la presentazione dei conti trimestrali, il presidente del board Harvey Jones aveva escluso il reintegro, mentre la Silicon Valley chiedeva il ritorno del fondatore anche con una petizione firmata da migliaia di dipendenti di Nvidia.

Colette Kress, CEO ad interim in queste settimane, rimarrà direttrice finanziaria (CFO). Jones resta presidente del consiglio; mentre l'indagine del comitato di amministratori indipendenti proseguirà fino alla conclusione .

Nvidia ha anche creato un comitato per la sicurezza nazionale e il controllo delle esportazioni. Inoltre è alla ricerca un Chief Compliance Officer , un ruolo nuovo per l'azienda, che dovrà controllare il rispetto delle regole in tutto il gruppo e riferirà al comitato del consiglio che si occupa di nomine e governance.

items.title: Building a wireless network adapter for the Super Nintendo
items.summary: Article URL: https://boland.dev/snet/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50611861 Points: 74 # Comments: 17
items.content:
I always come back to the Super Nintendo (SNES). It was my first console and it’s still my most potent source of nostalgia. It inspired my early interest in electronics as a teenager, designing circuits for mods and flash carts that I hoped to build one day. I followed the launch of Hackaday, Adafruit, and the progress of bunnie Huang’s Chumby and knew exactly what I wanted to do.

I dropped out of my final years of high school to study hands-on electronics at college, and continued on to university. Then, finally equipped with those skills I’d aspired to, I went off-track and spent the next fifteen years working in data, ML and software. A lot has changed in that time but I’m back now, picking up exactly where I left off.

The Super Network Adapter is an exercise in ‘16-bit futurism’, it aims to be a faithful peripheral to the original SNES hardware and what we imagined the future might be back then: a wireless link to the net, sync’ing saves across devices and an uplink to AI.

The SNES never had a dedicated network port. The closest it came was the Satellaview , a modem peripheral connected to a hidden expansion port that could receive game broadcasts via satellite. There was also the XBAND , a modem that plugged into the cartridge slot and supported pass-through patching of specific games for online play. Reproducing the hardware of either of these today would be challenging , however most peripherals for the SNES took a much simpler route, they used one of the controller ports.

The SNES controller ports are small synchronous serial buses that a game can control, setting and reading individual lines and driving the clock. These ports have seven lines but in a typical controller cable, only five tend to be present, with the wires for D1 and IOBit left out. To make sourcing parts for this project easier, my design also only relies on the remaining five wires.

First I needed a protocol for talking over this serial link, which I iterated with Mesen and a virtual network adapter written in Lua simulating the controller port link. This protocol has the SNES writing to the Latch line and reading from the adapter on D0 , one bit at a time (‘bit-banging’). Even with some optimisation (unrolling loops and ignoring mid-stream replies) this approach tops out at about 30 KB/s, but that’s enough for the ’90s.

The first physical prototype was built using a Pico 2 W dev board. The additional circuitry needed was very simple, just some pull-up resistors for CLK and Latch . The board’s RP2350A can handle the console’s 5v logic on its pins directly, and it has two cores: one can maintain the console link, while the other maintains the Wi-Fi network link, without juggling interrupts.

The prototype runs from USB, with the console’s 5v only feeding the pull-ups. I did not connect the SNES 5v to the Pico’s VBUS or VSYS while USB is plugged in. The Pico was powered on before the console so the RP2350’s pins were ready to handle 5v. The PCB design later can run on either supply.

Adding Cloud Save or ‘Save Sync’ seemed the most practical use for a Wi-Fi connection. I often go back to the SNES and start a new game, but if I could continue playing that save file in RetroArch on my phone and then back to the SNES, it would fit into my life much more easily.

Game save data is stored in battery-backed SRAM and in order for a game to send that through my adapter, I needed some of my own code to run. I already have a programmable flash cart for the SNES, so I wrote a utility to patch ROMs and inject this ‘save sync’ code into the reset vector. At power-on and whenever the console is reset, it syncs the save data through the adapter to a WebDAV server as saves/ / .srm (the same path RetroArch uses) so the console save can be continued on the phone, and vice versa.

First though, the adapter needs to join the local Wi-Fi network. I wanted an era-appropriate UI that can be run from a setup ROM (fig.2), which has you pick a network and type its password with an on-screen keyboard, one letter at a time. That felt most ‘authentic’ but I also made a second iteration that shows the typical QR code on the TV for setup via mobile phone.

The second version has the adapter set up a temporary network. Scanning the QR code with a phone joins the network and it then does the usual captive portal flow to open the adapter’s setup page, where the network and WebDAV auth details can be input in a much more user-friendly way.

An important detail to get right was checking whether the save on the cartridge was newest, or whether to download a newer one from WebDAV. RetroArch keeps a manifest file with a hash of every save, so the adapter updates that too, comparing hashes to decide whether the cartridge or the server has the newest save. If both sides have changed, nothing is overwritten and the cartridge’s save goes to a conflicts folder to play it safe.

SRAM saves are small but this sync still has to run whenever a game starts, potentially introducing a delay. To avoid this, the save is split into chunks that each have their own checksum, so only the chunks that have changed are sent over the controller port. In practice this makes the save sync delay imperceptible, and only when an existing save is pulled by the SNES for the first time is there a 1-2s load screen.

Naturally in 2026, an internet connection also means a connection to LLMs. The dialogue in SNES-era games tends to be fixed and unresponsive. In A Link to the Past, the villagers don’t react when you smash their pots (unlike in subsequent Zelda games). With the network adapter though, we can hook the game’s dialogue text renderer to swap out the original text for an in-character line generated by an LLM.

In order to prompt for dialogue, the LLM needs to be passed the game context, such as the character being interacted with and recent events. Since Link to the Past has been fully disassembled, it was possible to patch it to accumulate this state in RAM and push it out over the controller serial to the adapter and on to an LLM (via a proxy I ran on a local machine that holds the API key).

I tried a few different models and settled on Claude Opus 5.5, as cheaper models would break character or leak spoilers despite being prompted not to. I used LLM as a Judge evals to measure the proportion of responses that fit the context - Haiku scored 66%, Sonnet 90% and Opus 98%. The challenge was the time to first token of the LLM, for Haiku it was about 0.8 s but for Opus it averaged 2.2 s.

To avoid game-breaking delays from the LLM response times, I switched to speculatively generating the dialogue when Link approaches an NPC, storing the responses in a cache and invalidating them as the context updates. The delay from using a larger model was hidden and most NPC interactions had the response ready. This is a great way to burn tokens so probably not something to do for the full game duration!

When designing the PCB version of the adapter (fig.0) I replicated the same architecture as the prototype, an RP2350A microcontroller that handles the 5v lines and maintains the serial link, with an ESP32-C3 Wi-Fi coprocessor that handles the Wi-Fi connection. These communicate with each other over UART, allowing each link to be maintained by a dedicated core.

A PIO state machine on the RP2350 watches clock and latch , queueing the data and filtering out glitches shorter than 100 ns. This frees up the cores to prepare data to be sent over D0 while also talking to the C3.

The USB socket was included not just for flashing the board but also to support debugging it while it is powered from the SNES. This means the board needs to safely support taking a 5v supply from either the controller port or USB, and avoid backfeeding if both are connected. This is done with a LM66200 dual ideal diode. Supply can be taken from either source and we avoid the voltage drop that would come with using actual diodes. I’d seen some brownouts in tests on the breadboard, so designed the PCB with plenty of headroom for the LDO regulator even if the supply rail sags on a Wi-Fi burst.

While prototyping I also had issues when using series resistors on the link lines. This may be related to erratum RP2350-E9 in the A2 revision (stepping) of the RP2350A on my Pico 2 W. In the assembled PCB order I switched these to 0 Ω links, as they’re just for protection and I wasn’t sure which stepping the PCB would be assembled with. The boards turned out to have the fixed A4 stepping, so real resistors can go in next time.

The case is just a tray and a lid that sandwich the PCB, though I did want it to nod toward an era-appropriate design language. It was generated in code ( build123d ) using the PCB’s STEP files from KiCad, so that the design could be tested within a single 3D model.

The two halves join around the cable and the USB socket, and there are M2 pillars that align with the drilled holes in the PCB to hold everything together.

Since the PCB has a status LED, this design has a light pipe that channels that light up to become the dot of the etched Wi-Fi icon. It’s not the prettiest of designs, but I thought that was cute.

items.title: Il Black Friday LG è una vera svolta: più compri e più risparmi. Extra sconto fino al 20% e paghi da febbraio 2027
items.summary: Fino al 2 dicembre, i Member LG possono ottenere uno sconto crescente acquistando più prodotti: si parte dal 5% con un articolo e si arriva al 15% da tre prodotti in su. Ed è cumulabile con un ulteriore coupon del 5% ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Il Black Friday può essere l'occasione per sostituire un singolo prodotto, ma diventa ancora più interessante quando gli acquisti da fare sono diversi. Ma la paura è sempre quella di doversi poi confrontare con una spesa complessiva più grande del previsto.

Ecco perché LG ha deciso di proporre una promozione speciale per il Black Friday : più prodotti si aggiungono al carrello, maggiore diventa lo sconto applicato al checkout.

Fino al 2 dicembre, i clienti iscritti al programma Member possono ottenere uno sconto extra del 5% acquistando un prodotto, che sale al 10% con due prodotti e al 15% quando nel carrello se ne trovano almeno tre. L'iscrizione al programma è gratuita e può essere fatta online in pochi minuti .

Con un prodotto lo sconto applicato al checkout è del 5%; acquistandone due sale al 10%, mentre da tre prodotti in su raggiunge il 15% . L'elenco completo dei prodotti LG coinvolti nella promozione è disponibile alla pagina dedicata .

A questa riduzione può aggiungersi il coupon di benvenuto o di bentornato del 5% previsto per i Member LG idonei .

Combinando le due iniziative, lo sconto extra può quindi arrivare complessivamente fino al 20%.

Si tratta di una promozione vantaggiosa nel caso di acquisti che normalmente vengono pianificati insieme. Chi sta rinnovando la cucina, per esempio, può avere bisogno contemporaneamente di forno, lavastoviglie e frigorifero; allo stesso modo, chi sta aggiornando la propria postazione può abbinare un nuovo monitor ad altri prodotti LG, come una soundbar o dei nuovi auricolari wireless.

Ma c'è di più. Per i prodotti e gli acquisti che rispettano le condizioni previste, LG mette a disposizione il finanziamento a tasso zero, con la possibilità di iniziare a pagare da febbraio 2027 .

Il finanziamento a tasso zero è una delle modalità che LG propone sul proprio shop online anche durante il periodo del Black Friday, con piani da 10, 20 e 30 mesi sui prodotti selezionati e previa approvazione della finanziaria.

L'iniziativa "Tu aggiungi. Noi togliamo" è valida fino al 2 dicembre .

Fra i prodotti coinvolti nella promozione ci sono diverse categorie: TV, audio, cura dei capi, frigoriferi, cucina e informatica. Significa che la quantità e l'eterogeneità di prodotti inclusi è davvero elevata:

I prezzi indicati nell’articolo sono quelli rilevati al momento della sua predisposizione e potrebbero subire variazioni. Per conoscere il prezzo aggiornato e le condizioni applicabili, si invita a consultare la relativa pagina prodotto sullo shop online LG.

Fra i TV spicca sicuramente l'OLED evo AI G6 2026 da 65" . Il prezzo proposto ai Member LG è di 2.204,02 euro, a cui viene applicato uno sconto fra il 5 e il 20% a seconda della quantità di prodotti al carrello e della composizione di ulteriori bonus. In altre parole, il prezzo finale può scendere fino a 1.763 euro .

Il G6 utilizza il pannello Primary RGB Tandem 2.0 di LG Display, evoluzione di quello introdotto con il G5, e il nuovo processore Alpha 11 AI Gen3, che porta l'elaborazione video a 12 bit e punta soprattutto a migliorare la precisione nelle sfumature, riducendo il rischio di banding.

Un secondo TV molto interessante è l'OLED AI B6 Pro da 55" , che per i Member costa 979,03 euro.

Sfrutta il processore Alpha 7 Gen3 per analizzare i contenuti e ottimizzarli con interventi specifici. Con 8,3 milioni di zone destinate al dimming, il nero è davvero perfetto. E per i più appassionati, si può giocare ai videogiochi a risoluzione 4K fino a 120 FPS, senza tearing grazie al supporto di VRR, G-Sync e FreeSync Premium.

Con il massimo sconto applicabile il prezzo finale può scendere fino a 783,22 euro.

La Sound Suite H7 , proposta per i Member a 979,03 (ulteriormente da scontare a carrello), è una sounbar all in one, quindi non ha bisogno di ulteriori dispositivi.

In più, è anche compatibile con Dolby Atmos, il sistema di audio a oggetti che immerge lo spettatore nelle scene dei film e delle serie TV che lo supportano.

Anche in questo caso, cumulando il massimo sconto possibile (il 20%) il prezzo finale scende a 783,22 euro.

Per la cura dei capi, un'ottima proposta è la lavatrice smart Serie X5 da 11 kg , in classe energetica A-40%. La centrifuga arriva a 1.400 giri, è un elettrodomestico connesso via Wi-Fi 6 e con la funzionalità AI Wash, è l'Intelligenza Artificiale ad aiutare a scegliere il programma di lavaggio migliore sulla base dei capi e dei tessuti. Per i Member il prezzo di partenza (da scontare ulteriormente) è di 587,02 euro; con i vari sconti si può scendere fino a 469,61 euro.

Fra gli altri elettrodomestici coinvolti nella promozione LG per il Black Friday 2026 c'è il frigorifero combinato Fit & Max da 60 cm in Classe A da 375 litri è di 882,99 euro. Grazie alla funzione AI Inverter, l'Intelligenza Artificiale imparare dalle abitudini di utilizzo del frigorifero per raggiungere la freschezza ottimale degli alimenti e consumare in modo intelligente. Per chi accumula lo sconto massimo il prezzo scende a 706,39 euro.

Il forno a vapore Instaview da 76 litri in Classe A++ è altresì parte della promozione per il Black Friday: per i Member LG il prezzo è di 832,02 euro, da scontare in base alla composizione del carrello. La tecnologia Instaview permette di dare una rapida occhiata all'interno semplicemente bussando due volte sul vetro.

Sono incluse 22 modalità di cottura e con la tecnologia Blue EasyClean in appena dieci minuti il forno è pulito senza usare detersivi: merito della superficie con speciale smalto blu e allo specifico programma di pulizia.

E per chi è interessato a un nuovo monitor da gaming, l'UltraGear OLED 27" Quad HD (2560 x 1440) è proposto ai Member LG a 411,60 euro. È compatibile con G-Sync, VRR e FreeSync Premium, la frequenza di aggiornamento arriva a 240 Hz e include due porte HDMI 2.1 oltre a una DisplayPort 1.4.

In occasione del Black Friday, il prezzo finale può scendere fino a 329,28 euro.

items.title: NariQ: BF16-level Qwen3.8-27B in a 10 GB file
items.summary: We built NariQ: 3-bit-or-lower quantizations of Qwen3.8-27B that retain near-BF16 quality across agentic tasks, math, multilingual reasoning, and image understanding. To our knowledge, this is the first 3-bit-or-lower quantization that retains BF16 lvl performance on long-horizon agentic tasks. Benchmarks (BF16 / 3-bit / 2.5-bit / 2-bit): - DeepSWE: 39.8 / 41.0 / 41.9 / 28.6 - Terminal-Bench 2.1: 62.6 / 63.8 / 60.2 / 52.4 - AIME 25+26: 97.7 / 98.3 / 96.5 / 86.0 - MSGM: 94.0 / 93.1 / 91.8 / 90.6 - RealWorldQA: 82.4 / 82.4 / 81.3 / 80.9 Decode speed is comparable to other quants on an RTX PRO 60
items.content:
We built NariQ: 3-bit-or-lower quantizations of Qwen3.8-27B that retain near-BF16 quality across agentic tasks, math, multilingual reasoning, and image understanding.

To our knowledge, this is the first 3-bit-or-lower quantization that retains BF16 lvl performance on long-horizon agentic tasks.

Benchmarks (BF16 / 3-bit / 2.5-bit / 2-bit):

- DeepSWE: 39.8 / 41.0 / 41.9 / 28.6

- Terminal-Bench 2.1: 62.6 / 63.8 / 60.2 / 52.4

- AIME 25+26: 97.7 / 98.3 / 96.5 / 86.0

- MSGM: 94.0 / 93.1 / 91.8 / 90.6

- RealWorldQA: 82.4 / 82.4 / 81.3 / 80.9

Decode speed is comparable to other quants on an RTX PRO 6000. Context-length results below

(3-bit / 2.5-bit / 2-bit / Unsloth UD-IQ3_XXS):

- 4K: 88.9 / 99.2 / 111.7 / 94.7

- 16K: 84.5 / 93.8 / 105.1 / 89.8

- 64K: 70.7 / 77.5 / 85.0 / 74.8

Running these currently require our llama.cpp fork: (https://github.com/nari-labs/nari-llama.cpp)

Feedback and questions welcome. We'd love to hear how these perform on your workloads.

items.title: India pledges $1.6bn to Nepal in reset of ties
items.summary: As Nepal rebuilds after deadly floods, its prime minister sets contentious issues aside to secure Indian funding, port access and a new train service.
items.content:
Nepal's Prime Minister Balen Shah has repeatedly called for his country to be treated as an equal by its powerful neighbours. His first visit to the Indian capital, Delhi, put that approach to the test, as both sides sought to reset a relationship strained by years of friction.

Shah, 36, wearing his trademark black suit and sunglasses, stood beside Prime Minister Narendra Modi, 76, dressed in white. Shah rose to power after a wave of Gen Z-led protests toppled his predecessor.

Modi, meanwhile, is serving a third term and has recently faced student-led protests in India.

Yet, the two leaders seemed determined to project warmer relations. They exchanged gifts, inspected a military guard of honour and jointly flagged off a new cross-border train service.

For Nepal, the stakes were about far more than repairing diplomatic ties.

The two countries announced a series of agreements covering trade, hydropower, transport and education for Nepali youths.

India, more crucially, unveiled a $1.6bn (£1.22bn) support package as Nepal recovers from devastating floods earlier this year.

The floods killed more than 1,400 people, with thousands still missing. Shah's government has faced criticism over support for families which lost homes and loved ones.

The country faces a huge reconstruction challenge. The government estimates rebuilding could cost as much as $4.8bn. Addressing the UN General Assembly in September, Shah warned that when climate disasters devastate poorer countries, "the answer cannot simply be another mega-loan".

Modi pledged nearly $1.6bn in Indian support. Most of it will come as a line of credit for energy projects, alongside about $400m in grants for reconstruction and infrastructure.

While Nepal would have preferred a larger package, former senior Nepali diplomat Vijay Kant Karna says it is still "a significant amount" and could help stabilise a relationship that has often been uneasy.

A Hindu-majority nation wedged between India and China, Nepal has long had to navigate competing interests from its two giant neighbours. Allegations of political interference and an unresolved border dispute have frequently complicated ties with India.

Nepal's former Prime Minister, KP Sharma Oli, who leads a communist party, was widely viewed as being closer to China. Shah, by contrast, emerged as a political outsider when he was elected earlier this year. The former rapper, then 35, led a party that was only four years old.

His new approach of dealing with India may explain why the border dispute was largely absent from the leaders' public remarks, although the joint statement acknowledged that outstanding issues remained.

According to Govind Pokharel, a former vice-chairman of Nepal's National Planning Commission, Shah's government may have chosen to set contentious issues aside in order to secure progress on more immediate development needs.

"Right now you can go home and convince the young Nepalis that it will be handled later," Pokhrel says, "but if they don't deal with these issues in the future, there will be criticism."

Veteran Indian diplomat Anil Trigunayat says both sides appear to have opted to leave the dispute to established mechanisms rather than engage in what he calls "cartographic aggressions".

There were other gains for Nepal as a result of the Delhi visit.

As a landlocked country heavily dependent on India for trade, Nepal secured access to two additional Indian ports, Kandla and Paradip. The two sides also agreed to improve road and rail connectivity.

The leaders jointly inaugurated a train service linking Ayodhya in India, revered by Hindus as the birthplace of Lord Ram, with Janakpur in Nepal, traditionally regarded as the birthplace of his wife Sita.

Nepal has long sought greater access to Indian airspace in order to attract international traffic to its airports at Bhairahawa and Pokhara.

Some analysts believe the lack of an agreement reflects Indian concerns over Chinese involvement in the two airport projects.

"The airport in Pokhara can pose certain security challenges for India, so it is a more complicated issue to resolve," says Trigunayat.

India did, however, agree to make an existing air route linking Kathmandu, Bhairahawa and Lucknow bidirectional.

"Nepal invested a huge amount of money in those airports," says Pokharel. "It fell short of expectations, but the bidirectional route is a breakthrough."

Shah must now manage relations with China as he seeks to balance the interests of Nepal's two much larger neighbours.

For now he returns home with substantial financial commitments from India as Nepal continues the long task of rebuilding.

items.title: Flights cancelled in Belgium due to cost-of-living strike
items.summary: A series of strikes have hit Belgium in recent months as the prime minister struggles to agree a budget to cut costs.
items.content:
Hundreds of flights have been cancelled and public transport severely disrupted across Belgium as a result of a strike against planned austerity measures.

All air traffic has been halted at Brussels Airport in Zaventem as well as at Charleroi, home to low-cost airlines such as Ryanair.

Underground services have also been halted in capital Brussels, where large numbers of people joined a protest march.

The protest comes as Prime Minister Bart De Wever continues talks with his coalition allies over a budget to cut borrowing costs. King Philippe declined his resignation earlier this month, giving De Wever more time to negotiate.

No flights are taking off or landing at Brussels Airport between 07:00 and 21:00 local time (06:00-20:00 GMT) as a result of the strike by air traffic controllers.

"In total, 404 flights today cannot be operated, which has an impact on more than 50,000 passengers," Brussels Airport spokesperson Jeffrey Franssens said.

Reuters news agency spoke to Florence Faure, a French passenger who had arrived in Brussels from China's capital, Beijing, only to find that her flight to Paris Charles de Gaulle airport had been cancelled.

"Since our luggage was supposed to go on to Paris Charles de Gaulle, we didn't even collect it," she said.

A similar situation has affected Charleroi, where all flights were shown as "scheduled", regardless of the time of departure or arrival.

One passenger told Belgian broadcaster RTBF that she had received no warning and only discovered there were no flights when she arrived at the airport.

Philippe Naime, a teacher, was one of the tens of thousands taking part in the protest march in Brussels.

"Quite simply, no more money is being invested in education, and people are left to fend for themselves. But people do not have the means to do that," he told Reuters.

Public transport, schools and other public services are also facing disruptions.

One of its members, the socialist Vooruit, has been refusing to endorse plans agreed by the other four. It wants to raise taxes on the rich and for there to be fewer cuts to pensions and the health sector.

De Wever met King Philippe on Monday for the third update since the impasse.

"While expressing regret over the lack of significant progress, the king encouraged the prime minister to persevere in order to reach an agreement as soon as possible," the royal palace said in a statement.

The leader of one of the country's main unions, FGTB, said the government had alternatives to "dismantling the social protection system".

Bert Engelaar, head of the union, called for "a genuine wealth tax, fair taxation, and the elimination of tax loopholes".

"Political responsibility is not about keeping a government afloat at all costs. It's about knowing when to stop," he added, praising the Vooruit party.

Another union leader, Ann Vermorgen of the CSC, criticised government plans to cut bank holidays when they fall on weekends.

items.title: Mozilla contro Apple: dopo tre anni di DMA su iPhone non esiste nemmeno un browser non WebKit
items.summary: Mozilla esce allo scoperto: non è possibile realizzare un browser alternativo “vero” per iPhone a causa delle restrizioni di Apple. Che non può però nominare, perché protette da una clausola di riservatezza. ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Oggi chi usa Chrome, Firefox o Edge su iPhone non sta realmente usando Chrome, Firefox o Edge: sta solo usando Safari con un’altra interfaccia.

Apple, infatti, ha storicamente imposto a tutti i browser iOS il proprio motore di rendering, WebKit, e solo qualche anno fa in Europa grazie al Digital Markets Act sono state poste delle regole per rompere questo schema .

Apple si è adeguata e ha creato BrowserEngineKit, un set di API pensato proprio per i motori di navigazione alternativi, eppure, a distanza di quasi tre anni, in Europa nessuna azienda che realizza browser è riuscita a lanciare un browser non-WebKit su iOS.

Mozilla, con un post pubblicato qualche giorno fa sul suo blog , parla di condizioni “unworkable”, ovvero impossibili da soddisfare, aggiungendo però che, essendo vincolata da una clausola di riservatezza, non può entrare nei dettagli. Ci siamo incuriositi, abbiamo provato a cercare quali siano le condizioni di Apple e abbiamo visto che molte di queste sono comunque pubbliche.

Le prime sono soprattutto tecniche: il motore del browser deve dimostrare di essere completo e aggiornato, deve superare almeno il 90% dei Web Platform Tests, ovvero le prove con cui si controlla se un browser rispetta gli standard del web, e deve superare anche l’80% dei test JavaScript, richiesta sensata, visto che JS è il linguaggio che fa funzionare le pagine interattive. C’è però una clausola in più: Apple chiede che i test vengano superati anche senza JIT, che è quel componente che traduce al volo JavaScript in istruzioni per il processore, ed è il motivo per cui i browser moderni sono veloci. Per quanto sia utile, JIT è anche uno dei punti di accesso preferiti dai malware per entrare nel telefono, e proprio per questo motivo iOS lo spegne quando si attiva la Modalità di isolamento: il browser deve funzionare correttamente anche in quella condizione. Poi ci sono anche altri requisiti di sicurezza: la parte del motore che legge le pagine web, che è quella più esposta ai siti malevoli, deve essere scritta in linguaggi “memory-safe” o con accorgimenti che ne aumentino la sicurezza, e il browser deve anche sfruttare soluzioni di protezione hardware dei chip Apple. Inoltre il motore del browser deve separare le sue componenti in processi isolati, così che una pagina compromessa resti chiusa nel suo recinto, e deve correggere entro circa 30 giorni le falle già sfruttate dagli attaccanti.

Va detto che, per quanto siano richieste molto precise e impegnative, l’Open Web Advocacy, solitamente critica verso Apple, ha ritenuto che buona parte di queste regole di sicurezza sia ragionevole . L’unica condizione posta da OWA è che valgano anche per Safari, altrimenti diventano un ostacolo imposto solo ai concorrenti.

Il vero problema è un altro, ovvero l’app separata. Apple chiede che l’app con motore alternativo sia un’altra app distribuita solo in UE, non la stessa app che viene distribuita in tutto il mondo , dove Apple non deve rispettare le regole europee. Questo vuol dire che Mozilla non può semplicemente aggiornare Firefox, ma deve pubblicare un’app nuova che partirebbe con zero installazioni, zero recensioni e zero storico . Gli utenti hanno già scelto il loro browser dalla schermata di scelta, e magari hanno scelto Firefox: questi utenti sarebbero costretti a migrare da Firefox a Firefox, e in questo passaggio molti potrebbero anche scegliere di cambiare browser.

Mozilla, nel suo blogpost, dice chiaramente che non intende arrendersi, ricordando che dal 2024, da quando il DMA obbliga Apple a proporre la schermata di scelta del browser, milioni di europei hanno scelto Firefox e l’uso quotidiano del loro browser su iOS è raddoppiato. Questo nonostante questi utenti non possano avere Firefox completo, perché molte delle sue funzioni sono costruite dentro Gecko, il motore di Mozilla, che su Windows, Android e perfino su macOS c’è, ma su iPhone e iPad no. Per Mozilla il punto è proprio questo: se la Commissione ha messo una regola che, a distanza di tre anni, non ha cambiato nulla, quella regola deve essere rivista.

items.title: Droni a idrogeno verde trasportano materiali sanitari: il test a Padova
items.summary: Il drone cargo può trasportare 4 kg fino a 100 km. Nel 2027 sono previsti test per collegare diversi poli della logistica sanitaria del Veneto ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Produrre idrogeno verde in aeroporto e usarlo per rifornire droni destinati al trasporto di materiali sanitari urgenti. È il progetto Padova Sandbox, entrato nella fase operativa all’aeroporto civile Gino Allegri di Padova, gestito da Heron Air. I primi voli si svolgeranno all’interno dello scalo, mentre nel 2027 la sperimentazione dovrebbe estendersi ai collegamenti tra poli della logistica sanitaria del Veneto.

Il sistema parte da un impianto fotovoltaico da 50 kW installato nell’area di prova. L’elettricità prodotta alimenta il KEB, acronimo di Key Energy Builder, che produce, immagazzina ed eroga l’idrogeno verde destinato al drone cargo multicottero GH2. La componente tecnologica e operativa è affidata a H2G, divisione del Gruppo H2C specializzata nelle soluzioni per l’idrogeno verde.

Il drone può percorrere fino a 100 km, trasportare complessivamente quattro chilogrammi di materiali e raggiungere una velocità massima di 55 km/h .

Per un volo a pieno carico consuma circa 350 g di idrogeno, con un rifornimento che richiede dieci minuti.

Alla sperimentazione partecipa anche la software house veneta Stesi, partner di H2C per l’integrazione del sistema di supervisione. La sua piattaforma silwa sarà utilizzata per gestire i flussi logistici e coordinare la manutenzione ordinaria, straordinaria e predittiva dei sistemi impiegati.

" Il nostro contributo riguarda la supervisione dei flussi, la tracciabilità e la gestione della manutenzione: attività necessarie per coordinare mezzi, componenti e informazioni lungo il processo operativo ", ha spiegato Stefano Cudicio, presidente di Stesi.

È prevista l’integrazione dei dati dei sensori per monitorare le condizioni operative e segnalare gli allarmi. Il software gestirà inoltre i ricambi e la loro tracciabilità attraverso lotti e numeri di serie.

Il progetto è stato avviato a marzo 2025 nell’ambito dell’accordo sulla Mobilità Aerea Avanzata sottoscritto nel maggio 2024 da ENAC, Regione Veneto e Gruppo SAVE. La fase prevista per il 2027 comprende voli BVLOS, condotti senza contatto visivo diretto tra pilota e velivolo. Durante i test saranno monitorate le condizioni di trasporto del materiale sanitario in un contenitore refrigerato, la cui alimentazione utilizzerà l’idrogeno prodotto in aeroporto.

items.title: 'I want to destroy capitalism, not France': On the streets with the French ultra left
items.summary: The BBC meets the far-left protesters French President Emmanuel Macron says are trying to bring down the Republic.
items.content:
France is in turmoil. Crippling public debt, a "lame-duck" president with six months left in office, and massive social unrest - sparked by student protests which have erupted into looting and violence.

This Saturday marked the sixth weekend in a row of demos against soaring prices, worsening public services and alleged police brutality. Violence by protesters is down on last month but still present.

President Emmanuel Macron has publicly blamed riots on "delinquents" and "ultra-left groups" whose aim, he says, is to bring down the French Republic.

The unrest in France has become a political football ahead of key presidential and parliamentary elections next year. The left in France blames the centre and right for the cost-of-living crisis that's making French people so upset and angry. They blame the hard left for fomenting violence (which they deny). While the nationalist right pledges, if elected, it will return order and security to France's streets.

So, who exactly are these "ultra-left" groups Macron speaks of? And how organised and dangerous are they?

It's infamously hard to speak to members of the radical left. They don't much like what they call mainstream media. We're viewed as part of an establishment many of them despise.

My best bet was to head out into the protests and try to approach people dressed in all black and ski masks or balaclavas (worn, they say, to hide their identity from police). It's a quasi-uniform associated with left-wing rioters or disruptors, known as the Black Block.

You see them at demos all over Europe. In France, they tend to appear from city side streets, as daytime protests are dying down, dusk is falling and riot police begin to emerge in full force.

French intelligence drastically underestimated the outpouring of anger, looting and destruction following protests last month. More than 1,000 police officers were reportedly injured, young protesters had bones broken and two reportedly lost a hand in altercations with police armed with stun grenades. Le Monde newspaper has an article , external it is constantly updating to investigate a rising number of reports of protester injuries. The French Insurers Federation estimates damages to shops and private property on 17 October alone - the day of the biggest riots - came to around €207m (£175.5m).

Since then, the French authorities are trying to tightly manage demos. Police presence is heavy. Protesters say heavy handed.

Towards the end of one of the protests this month, we saw would-be rioters vastly outnumbered, glass bottles and homemade paint bombs at the ready to throw at police. They were no match for the batons, stun grenades and tear gas the officers had to hand.

As we were being forcefully kettled in by police, I tried to talk to would-be rioters. Few wanted to engage but I then met 18-year-old Nas (not his real name) and friends. They would only speak to me if they could hide their identity. This was to avoid police detection, they said.

Milling, you could say provocatively, by baton-at-the-ready police – they seemed to fit a radical-left rioter stereotype.

"Without violence, you don't achieve anything," one of them tells me. "It's the only way to get our voices heard."

"We come from an area with a bad reputation. Our schools are a mess. Our teachers quit. You need qualifications to get a decent job. There is supposed to be equality in France. We won't give up our fight."

These young men, we discover, come from the sprawling housing estates common on French city outskirts - the banlieues - associated with deprivation, unrest and second or third generation immigrant families.

They weren't politicised or organised by the radical left, they insisted. Just angry.

Earlier, I had spotted two hard-left student activists, standing masked on top of a bus shelter, above the thronging crowd of protesters waving banners sporting the red anarchist sign and the symbol for the Antifa (anti-fascist) movement.

I put it to them that France has a proud tradition and respect for the right to protest but that the country has been horrified by the violence it's seen over the last weeks.

They were keen to downplay the rioting but - again – would only speak if they could remain anonymous.

"Violence ends up reflecting badly on our movements. We don't like it. But what's a smashed shop window compared to police using stun guns on protesting school kids? Also, people [in France] are regularly going cold and hungry. They're losing faith in this society."

How could they believe violence would bring about a juster society, I wondered?

They shrug off my question. In France, these days, the real violence is state violence, they say.

French intelligence estimates there are 5,000 "ultra-left" activists in the country.

Anticapitalist Starflix (that's his codename) counts himself as one of them. The 17-year-old is also a member of the violent Black Block movement. We'd arranged to meet on the edge of the protest, by a narrow canal.

Fearful about being apprehended by police, he asked to remain anonymous.

He showed me a couple of homemade paint-bombs - eggshells filled with paint and sealed with medical tape that he throws at police officers. He carries them in his rucksack, wrapped in a royal blue Italia football shirt.

"We throw the paint bombs at the visors on riot police helmets, so they have to lift them up in order to see and that makes them suffer their own tear gas that they've sprayed at us," he tells me.

"We pick up stones and rocks too. Anything we find on the streets of Paris, to throw."

I put it to him that he and others in the Black Block are causing a lot of problems on French streets: damaging businesses, hurting police officers, destroying the demos for peaceful protesters. What is he trying to achieve?

As he's under 18, his parents give us permission to speak to him. They share his politics, Starflix tells me, but not all rioters - masked and dressed in black as he is - do.

"The Black Block isn't a single organisation. It's a technique. Some of us use violence to get government reform. I want to bring about a revolution.

"Other people are opportunists who use anonymity to steal things. When we all wear the same clothes, it makes it harder for police to identify us."

When I ask if he is scared he might get hurt or arrested, he admits he is but says what frightens him more is the thought that society might not change.

Social media plays a huge role in the riots. Starflix tells me he and his friends use Signal and Telegram to arrange to meet at protests.

There are numerous websites and Instagram profiles, mainly hosted by left-wing organisations, offering tips for protesters and rioters, such as: keep your phone at home so police can't track you, cover your face to avoid being identified and emulate martial arts expert Bruce Lee and "be like water" - appearing and disappearing into crowds. That's advice passed on by the Hong Kong protesters eight years ago.

While not formally organising the protests or violence with these posts, could the fact groups host this information online be viewed as a kind of incitement or manipulation of youngsters whose feelings are running so high in France?

All the young rioters I spoke to insist they are not being herded or directed, but is there something bigger behind what's happening?

It takes our team a long time, but they manage to find a seasoned activist with the Black Block who would speak to us. I put to him Macron's assertion that the ultra left has organised groups that aim to bring down the French Republic. Is that true?

"It's totally false of the authorities to say we are all organised. And the intelligence services know it," the activist scoffs. "It's a manipulation of the French public to make them think there is an enemy within."

"Basically, people turn up to a protest, get dressed in black and do their own thing. The uniting factor is rage and not just in France. You see the same rage [in protests] in Italy, Germany, Spain. It's exploding by itself."

I ask if the anti-capitalist presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon and his France Unbowed party (LFI) are somehow linked to the violence. They are present at most protests, supporters handing out campaign pamphlets to the chanting crowds.

But the activist denies this, telling me Mélenchon is "a capitalist because he's part of the system". He says the LFI and the trade unions try to "calm" unrest, while he believes things need to be "stepped up a notch".

Why had he decided to talk to us, I ask - does he want to collapse the French government?

"I just want to say we don't love violence. I don't want to destroy France. We want to destroy a system that is a capitalist system, of course, but to change the society in a way that we think will be better for the most people, for more people.

"More and more find it hard to make ends meet. In the countryside, people can't even afford to fill their tank with petrol."

You have to leave the city, heading out into the gloriously autumnal French countryside, to meet some of the more organised, hardcore elements of the ultra left.

items.title: Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 after flipping North Carolina seat
items.summary: Democrats have now won at least 258 seats in the midterms compared to Republicans, who hold at least 173 seats.
items.content:
The Democratic Party has won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives since 1992, after Democrat Chuck Hubbard unseated Republican Representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina.

The race was called on Sunday, with Hubbard beating Foxx by 330 votes with 99% counted. It was one of the closest contests of the recent midterm elections, in which Democrats also secured the Senate.

The party has now won at least 258 House seats in the midterms compared to Republicans, who hold at least 173 seats, with four races still yet to be called.

Neither party had won as many House races since 1992, when Bill Clinton won the presidency and Democrats won a total of 258 seats.

Sunday's result came after Foxx, who has represented North Carolina's 5th Congressional District since 2005, requested a recount. This is allowed under state law when the margin of victory is under 1%.

"I think the American people are just sick of what's going on and they wanted a change. They voted for change," Hubbard told the BBC News Channel after his victory. He pledged to work alongside his fellow lawmakers to hold President Donald Trump accountable.

Earlier, he wrote on X that he had spoken to Foxx, "who graciously conceded following the results of the recount process".

Hubbard added: "I deeply appreciate her commitment to a smooth transition of the office and constituent casework. We may not always agree, but we both love North Carolina and the people of the Fifth District."

Foxx, meanwhile, said in a statement: "After running a campaign focused on my track record of commonsense solutions and conservative values, I'm humbled and grateful that so many North Carolina voters responded by supporting my candidacy, even if we came up just a few votes short."

Hubbard's win, which comes after he lost to Foxx two years ago by nine percentage points, followed a number of Democratic victories in deeply Republican districts including South Carolina, Texas, Alaska and Iowa.

Hubbard, like many Democrats running in the midterms, focused on the rising cost of living in the US during the war with Iran - a top issue for voters.

Trump himself - as well as Vice President JD Vance - have suggested inflation caused by the war in Iran was probably to blame for the Republican losses.

Hubbard has also said he will also prioritise working families and small businesses, supporting public education and expanding access to affordable healthcare, according to his website.

The remaining House races yet to be called are in Tennessee and Minnesota, while two elections in Louisiana will go to a runoff in December. In Tennessee's fourth district, Democrat Victoria Broderick leads by fewer than 300 votes, and in Minnesota's first district, Democrat Jake Johnson is winning by fewer than 500 votes.

Democrats may use their upcoming majority in the House and control of the Senate to investigate conflicts of interest and other actions by the president and those close to him, while the Senate also has the power to confirm or block the president's cabinet and judicial nominations. They will also be able to pass legislation through Congress easily, though Trump still has to give final sign off for it to become law.

However, even with control of both chambers of Congress, they will still have limits on their power as Trump can veto legislation.

items.title: Search and rescue teams race against time to find survivors after Nigeria boat tragedy
items.summary: The government blames overcrowding, poor maintenance, and missing life jackets for boat accidents.
items.content:
Nigerian search and rescue teams are racing against time to find survivors after a boat carrying mourners travelling to a funeral capsized on Friday.

Twenty-nine bodies have been recovered and 50 people rescued so far, a spokesperson for the National Emergency Management Agency (Nema) told the BBC.

The government has responded by ordering stricter enforcement of safety standards on the country's inland waterways.

Overcrowding, poor maintenance and failure to observe safety regulations have contributed to previous deadly accidents on Nigeria's rivers.

The boat was travelling from Ayama community when it developed mechanical problems, according to police spokesperson Musa Mohammed.

Passengers asked the boat operator to steer towards land, but he allegedly declined, leading to the accident.

Survivors have described the panic that followed as passengers struggled to swim and stay afloat while waiting for emergency rescue services.

"As I swam, people were dragging me to the bottom, and I bit one woman and saved myself," Charity Ebikaboaere told local media outlet Arise News.

"Our things, our money, phones, everything lost, but me and my siblings are alive," said another survivor, Tari Samuel.

Nema spokesman Manzo Ezekiel raised concerns about the use of untrained boat operators and passengers travelling without life jackets.

"Some of them believe they're from river areas and they know how to swim," he said, warning that familiarity with waterways should not replace basic safety precautions.

There have been reports that the boat was carrying more than 300 people but the Nema spokesperson said this wasn't correct. He did not say how many people were on board but said it was overcrowded.

The accident happened in a region where waterways are a key means of transport, especially for communities with limited road access.

"Overloading, speeding, recklessness and traveling without life jackets must stop. No journey is worth a life," Bayelsa Commissioner for Information Ebiuwou Koku-Obiyai said in a statement on Saturday.

Nigeria's President Bola Tinubu has relayed his condolences to the victims' families.

In a statement posted on X, Tinubu said he had directed relevant federal disaster response agencies to work together to ensure a successful rescue and recovery operation.

He also ordered that his election rally on Saturday, in Ibadan, Oyo State, be held without much fanfare in honour of those who lost their lives.

Boat accidents are a recurring problem in Nigeria, particularly in riverine communities where boats are a major means of transport.

In August, at least 50 people, mostly children, died after an overloaded boat capsized in the north-western Sokoto state. In January, at least 25 people died when a leaking boat capsized in Yobe state, in the north-east.

items.title: Win4wine – Run Windows Shell as the Linux Desktop on Wine
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/mikuta0407/win4wine Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50610743 Points: 200 # Comments: 104
items.content:
個人の実験的なプロジェクトです。 日常の作業環境として使えるほど完成してはいません。 動作を確かめているのは、 新しくインストールした Debian 13 に導入スクリプトで入れた場合だけです。 すでに使っている環境（ほかのデスクトップ環境やディスプレイマネージャが入っているものなど）への導入は試していません。 試すときは、仮想マシンや試験用のマシンをおすすめします。

Windows XP の explorer.exe を、パッチを当てた Wine の上で Linux のデスクトップシェル として動かすプロジェクトです。 タスクバー、スタートメニュー、デスクトップ、フォルダウィンドウは XP 本物のものです。Linux のアプリも、XP の枠とタスクバーで扱えます。

Microsoft のファイルは同梱していません。お手元の XP の ISO から、必要なファイルだけを取り出して使います。

XP の ISO が無い方は、XP のシェルの代わりに ReactOS のシェル （Windows 2000 風のクラシックの見た目）でも 試せます。ReactOS は自由なソフトウェアなので、導入スクリプトが公式のリリースから取得します（ docs/reactos.md ）。

Windows 7 の ISO があれば、 Windows 7 のシェル （Windows 7 ベーシックの見た目）でも試せます。まだ実験的な試作です（ docs/windows7.md ）。

詳しい手順とオプションは 🔗 導入手順（INSTALL.md） にあります。Wine をソースからビルドするので、4 コアで 1 時間半ほどかかります。 テーマ（XP のクラシックなど）と文字の大きさは、後から変えられます（ 見た目と文字の大きさを変える ）。

LGPL-2.1-or-later （Wine と同じ）です。対象はこのリポジトリのコードとパッチだけです。 ただし wayland/patches/labwc/ は labwc と同じ GPL-2.0-only、 wayland/patches/wlroots/ は wlroots と同じ MIT です。 Windows XP と Windows 7 のファイルと、スクリーンショットに写っている XP と Windows 7 の画面の著作権は Microsoft にあります。 ReactOS のシェルで使う ReactOS のファイルは、ReactOS のライセンス（GPL-2.0-or-later、DLL の多くは LGPL-2.1-or-later）に従います。

items.title: Ci sono stati allarmi bomba in moltissime scuole in Germania e in Danimarca
items.content:
La polizia tedesca ha detto che lunedì mattina moltissime scuole in tutta la Germania hanno ricevuto mail di minaccia secondo cui sarebbero state piazzate delle bombe negli edifici. Anche la polizia della Danimarca ha detto che sta investigando su minacce ricevute da molte scuole. L’episodio ricalca quanto avvenuto in Italia all’inizio di novembre. Anche in questo caso, come in quello italiano , tutte le minacce si sono rivelate infondate.

La polizia della Danimarca e di molti stati federati tedeschi hanno detto di aver aperto delle indagini, anche se non ritenengono ci sia alcun pericolo per le scuole. In molti casi le minacce sono state ignorate, dopo che le scuole si erano consultate con la polizia, come prevede la procedura. Alcuni edifici sono stati comunque evacuati, e le lezioni sospese.
